title: RetireFlow: deprecation orchestrator + customer migration assistant for legacy model versions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build an end-to-end deprecation workflow (internal name: RetireFlow) that ties model onboarding, version pinning, and performance profile publishing into a single orchestrated experience for retiring old model versions. This ticket covers the product design and rollout plan for: 1) automated customer notification cadence, 2) an in-console Migration Assistant that recommends concrete pin targets (model + quantization + perf profile) derived from our published performance profiles, 3) SDK and API deprecation headers/warnings, 4) an opt-in auto-migration path for low-risk customers, and 5) observability/alerts for migration regressions.

Why this is different: existing playbooks focus on notices and migration guides. RetireFlow is an orchestration layer that programmatically maps each deprecated model-version to one or more recommended replacements using our performance profiles and cost heuristics, then drives customer communications and in-console actions with one-click or automated migration options. That reduces friction and helps meet our reliability and cost SLAs while minimizing customer surprise.
acceptance_criteria: A1: For a given model-version X deprecation, the system publishes a mapping file linking X -> set of recommended replacements with reason (latency delta, token cost estimate, quality delta).
A2: Console Migration Assistant surface exists behind feature flag: shows affected routes, recommended pin, one-click 'Pin for this route' and 'Schedule auto-migrate' actions.
A3: API returns deprecation header (X-Model-Deprecated: true) and SDK emits a standardized warning at runtime and during model load. Warnings include migration link and timeline.
A4: Notification cadence triggers emails/console banners at D-90/D-30/D-14/D-7 and final D-0 with links to migration guide and a step-by-step checklist.
A5: Automated migration job (opt-in) can migrate a sample of traffic for canary customers, validate token-cost and latency objectives against published perf-profile, and rollback on regression.
A6: Documentation page (migration guide) generated from templates and linked in notices; PR created in docs repo before first D-90 notice.

A7: Monitoring dashboards show migration adoption %, rollback events, error-rate delta, latency delta, and token-cost delta per-customer. Alerts fire when error-rate increases > 1.5x baseline or latency P95 regresses > 40%.
runbook_steps: Step 0: Gather model-version metadata (release date, owners, usage volume, perf profile snapshot).
Step 1: Compute candidate replacements using perf-profile matcher: rank candidates by quality-loss, cost delta, and latency delta. Export top-3 suggestions with justification strings.
Step 2: Internal review: PM + Research sign-off on top candidate list and regression risk assessment.
Step 3: Create migration mapping artifact and commit to /infra/model-deprecations repo (YAML mapping + perf diffs).
Step 4: Prepare docs & migration guide: auto-generate changelog, pinning instructions, SDK code samples (node/python/go), and recommended prompt adjustments.
Step 5: QA: run eval suite (customer prompt set spot checks) comparing old vs recommended models; record quality regressions and acceptable thresholds.
Step 6: Enable console feature flag for targeted beta (5 pilot customers) and run canary auto-migrate for up to 10% of traffic.
Step 7: Monitor metrics for 72 hours; if thresholds exceeded, rollback and create incident blameless postmortem.
Step 8: If canary successful, enable global notices (D-90 start) and open support ticket templates for high-touch customers.
notifications_timeline: D-90: Initial notice (email + console banner) with rationale, migration assistant link, and migration FAQ.
D-60: Follow-up reminder with estimated impact (per-route token cost estimate) and suggested pin target(s).
D-30: Migration guide published; one-click pinning available in console; release notes and SDK warning scheduled.
D-14: Last-call notice; offer support-session booking for enterprise customers and opt-in auto-migrate form.
D-7: Alert: scheduled deprecation date and potential fallback policy if auto-migration not complete.
D-0: Deprecation enacted: old model removed from new allocations; clients still calling get soft-fallbacks (if configured) and receive error+migration header.
automation_tasks: Create model-deprecation mapping generator (ENG-8246) that consumes performance profiles and outputs candidate suggestions.
Add job to infra pipeline to commit mapping file and trigger doc generation when 'deprecate' flag is set.
Console: implement Migration Assistant backend endpoints and 'pin' mutation; front-end banner component and feature flag gating.
SDKs: add deprecation header parser and standardized console warning text; publish v3.4.0 with opt-in auto-migration client API.
Support: template emails and support flow (Zendesk macros) with one-click escalation to Customer Success.
Telemetry: add 'migration.scheduled' and 'migration.completed' events with customer_id, route_id, baseline_metrics.
console_changes: Banner component showing deprecation status on model details and affected routes pages.
Migration Assistant modal: recommended pins, one-click pin action, schedule auto-migrate toggle, and failure-safe preview.
Per-route timeline UI (D-90..D-0) with customer adoption % and recommended action.
sdk_changes: Add X-Model-Deprecated header parsing and map to Migration Assistant URL in SDK warnings (node/python/go).
Add client method migrateModel(routeId, {targetModel, schedule, canaryPct}) for customers that opt-in to programmatic migration.
Update quickstarts to show pinning examples and new SDK warning behavior in error-handling best practices.
